summary.text: The paired verses describe the knower's inward non-doership while bodily and sensory activities continue. The I of that recognition is not a changing social role, and the conviction is not a mantra maintained by effort. Even blinking belongs to the senses functioning among their objects. The teacher holds ultimate non-agency together with transactional functioning without denying either its appropriate status. A long discussion probes role-based duty and whether realization is mental rewiring. The teacher accepts correction through the mind but insists the mind becomes known as an object; even a liberated-mind identity does not define the final knower.

segments.heading: Two verses form one account of inward recognition

blocks.text: The prior self-of-all recognition leads to the question of continued life. Krishna's paired verses describe inward non-doership across an extensive list of ordinary activities.
The negation is not merely doing less or being less attached. The teacher stresses the knower's first-person understanding that Atma is not an agent at all.

segments.heading: The recognized I is not a changing role

blocks.text: Age, occupation and family positions are changing identifications. The inward recognition concerns the self in whose presence activity appears, not a person loudly denying responsibility.

This conviction follows knowledge naturally rather than repeated mental effort. The teacher defines the truth-knower through self-Brahman identity and warns against reducing indicative terms to ordinary usage.
Let us retain it as tattva.

segments.heading: Even minute activities belong to the instruments

blocks.text: Seeing, eating, sleeping, speaking and blinking span voluntary and involuntary life. No minute activity escapes the distinction between its appearance and a claimed self-agent.
As dream events are understood differently on waking, the senses are recognized operating in their own respective domains. Their functioning belongs to Prakriti rather than a command issued by Atma.

segments.heading: Two standpoints remain clear without collapse

blocks.text: The first recognition concerns ultimate non-agency; the second concerns sensory functioning transactionally. Vyavahara is not outside reality, but its appearance does not turn Atma into an agent.
The knower neither denies that activity appears nor appropriates it. Discrimination preserves functional reality at its level without confusing it with the self's ultimate nature.

segments.heading: Abiding recognition is not a concentration technique

blocks.text: The teacher connects this inward account with the earlier outward description of the steady person. Background recognition continues during activity without being a separately maintained meditative exercise.
The commentary connects absence of self-agency with total renunciation. A mirage illustrates why one no longer pursues a mistaken object's supposed benefit after correction.

segments.heading: Roles and duties remain transactional appearances

blocks.text: A participant asks how voluntary roles and role-specific duty are directed. The teacher locates motherhood, employment and related duties in bodily and sensory functioning.
The knower sees these roles without making them self-nature. The dream comparison shifts the question from owning a role to recognizing the consciousness in which the role appears.

segments.heading: The rewiring analogy does not define the self

blocks.text: The participant proposes mental rewiring and a liberated mind as intermediate descriptions. The teacher resists identifying consciousness with intellect while accepting that correction proceeds through the mind.
When mind itself is known as an object, it cannot be the knowing self. The final distinction is not an individual possessing a better mind; even that subtle owner is relinquished.

segments.heading: Do not confuse the fact with its transactions

blocks.text: Follow-ups equate the steady person with the truth-knower and ask about a universal mind. The teacher maintains non-separateness rather than positing independently liberated souls alongside Ishwara.
Even scriptural formulations belong to transaction. The closing distinction is that appearances do not condition the reality in which they occur; scheduling then concludes the room.

concepts.label: tattva
concepts.gloss: The reality whose knower recognizes self rather than private agency.

concepts.label: Sakshi
concepts.gloss: Witness-awareness distinguished from the changing role.

concepts.label: Prakriti
concepts.gloss: The domain in which sensory functioning takes place.

concepts.label: viveka
concepts.gloss: Discrimination preserving the distinction between transactional and ultimate standpoints.

concepts.label: Amani Bhava
concepts.gloss: The participant's no-mind reference within the discussion of mental correction.

gaps.note: Local ASR alternates agent and non-agent; surrounding explicit non-doership governs paraphrase.
ASR renders thatness inconsistently; the teacher explicitly asks to retain tattva.
Another malformed self-agency phrase occurs beside the explicit non-doer gloss.
Mirage commentary Sanskrit is garbled; only the English illustration is summarized.
Extended exchange revises the participant's computer terminology; it is not presented as an agreed literal neural model.
